The core operational principle of RTK lies in resolving integer ambiguities in real-time using double-differenced carrier phase observations. These differenced measurements mitigate common-mode errors such as satellite clock offsets and atmospheric delays. By leveraging small wavelengths (19–24 cm), precise ranging becomes feasible. The process assumes a known stochastic behavior of unmodeled errors—such as multipath and noise—which can degrade performance. Statistical selection of the most probable solution requires evaluating all possible positions within a defined search box. This approach enables millimeter-level accuracy but demands robust cycle slip detection mechanisms due to its sensitivity to data interruptions and environmental degradation. The computational complexity increases significantly with more satellites, limiting scalability in dense urban or obstructed environments.
